source.title: Pseudo-Asynchronous Local SGD: Robust and Efficient Data-Parallel Training
source.authors: Hiroki Naganuma; Xin-Zhi Zhang; Man-Chung Yue; Ioannis Mitliagkas; P. Witte; Russell J. Hewett; Yin Lee

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies global batch size through GPU scaling under a fixed epoch budget and reports validation-accuracy changes. It also reports that PALSGD and DiLoCo retain higher validation accuracy than DDP while themselves losing accuracy at the largest scale, qualifying the large-batch generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are from CIFAR-10 on VGG-16 in Appendix F.1. Other optimizer, synchronization, and training-time results do not measure a claim version. Cited prior findings are not extracted as study results.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures held-out accuracy as global batch size increases under fixed epochs on CIFAR-10/VGG-16, testing V5 in a distributed setting. Its optimizer ablation also bears on V4, with qualifications about optimizer role and tuning.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Appendix F.1: the authors attribute DDP's sharp decline at 32 GPUs tentatively to large batches; PALSGD and DiLoCo also degrade but remain more accurate. Their broader conclusion is that PALSGD reduces communication and training time while maintaining competitive model performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales the global batch by increasing GPU count with epochs fixed, rather than directly comparing batch sizes at a fixed GPU configuration. It compares DDP, Local SGD variants, and PALSGD under CIFAR-10 image classification.
record.method_sensitivity: GPU count/global batch size changes validation accuracy; at 32 GPUs, both PALSGD and DiLoCo also show accuracy degradation, though they remain above DDP.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing synchronization interval, mixing strength, or pseudo-synchronization probability changes validation loss and runtime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Communication and local-update choices affect distributed training performance; these sweeps do not themselves vary batch size or measure another listed claim.

record.problems: The scale comparison also changes worker count and training steps; no same-model smaller-batch control at each scale is reported. The prose gives relative accuracy changes but not the underlying exact accuracy values. Experiments are described as using the largest possible per-GPU batch size.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version result rows were found. Figure F.1 contains plotted values for runtime and validation accuracy; exact plotted values were not reconstructed where the text did not state them.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.
Standalone Adam versus SGD under the specified limited-tuning protocol; matched training performance; switching optimizers; and controlled weight-decay comparisons.

Controlled language-model batch sweeps; longer training; and isolated effects of learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization. The distributed comparisons change worker count and update count along with batch size.
Dropout and weight-decay removal or strength ablations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Optimizer-role ablation: AdamW as outer optimizer substantially worsens validation loss, while AdamW inner optimization combined with Nesterov or momentum SGD achieves the best loss. Record matched inner/outer comparisons separately and document the tuning protocol.

VGG-16 comparison with smaller local batches: DDP validation accuracy is 89.80%, versus 91.34% for DiLoCo and 91.77% for PALSGD at H=32. The authors identify fourfold smaller update batches as a possible explanation. Algorithm and synchronization also change, so this is not an isolated batch-size intervention.
missing.locator: Appendix C.4, Figure C.5; Appendix B.1 specifies 200 epochs

record.verdict_notes: Higher accuracy than DDP does not justify the record's limits_scope verdict for V5: the methods still show the predicted scaling penalty. V4 evidence concerns optimizers inside PALSGD, with other hyperparameters held at selected values, so it does not establish the standalone limited-tuning comparison. No uncertainty is reported for the batch-scaling accuracy changes.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Language models, comparisons against smaller batches at a fixed model and workload, and the effects of longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons to other generalization measures.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Scaled DDP training across GPU counts, increasing global batch size while keeping total training epochs fixed.

conditions.value: Global batch increased proportionally; per-GPU batch size 256

rows.value: 4% drop in validation accuracy when scaled from 4 to 16 GPUs
rows.locator: Appendix F.1, text following Figure F.1
rows.note: The text reports the change but does not give the underlying accuracy values.
rows.check: The reported 4% accuracy decline clearly exhibits V5's penalty; partial is inappropriate. Global batch increases from 1,024 to 4,096. Learning rates were searched separately for each configuration, with no learning-rate decay.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Scaled DDP training across GPU counts, increasing global batch size while keeping total training epochs fixed.
rows.locator: Appendix F.1, text following Figure F.1
rows.note: The authors attribute the sharp decline likely to the large-batch problem; the text does not state the exact 32-GPU accuracy.
rows.check: The reported decline exceeding 15% clearly exhibits the penalty. Preserve the authors' percentage wording because relative percent versus percentage points is unspecified. The 4-GPU baseline is contextual rather than explicitly repeated in this sentence.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Scaled PALSGD and DiLoCo training across GPU counts, increasing global batch size while keeping total training epochs fixed.
rows.value: Both methods suffer accuracy degradation at 32 GPUs, but consistently achieve higher validation accuracy than DDP; PALSGD exceeds DiLoCo across all scales.
rows.locator: Appendix F.1, text following Figure F.1
rows.note: The text groups PALSGD and DiLoCo in the shared statement about degradation and higher accuracy; separate exact values are shown only in Figure F.1.
rows.check: Split PALSGD and DiLoCo into separate rows measuring their accuracy degradation at 32 GPUs relative to lower-GPU configurations. Their superiority to DDP is a separate algorithm comparison and does not itself measure the batch-size penalty. The text explicitly reports degradation for both, without its magnitude.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10/VGG-16, fixed epochs, 256 examples per GPU, scaling DDP from 4 to 16 and 32 GPUs
relationships.reason: R1 reports a 4% validation-accuracy decline and R2 a decline exceeding 15% as global batch increases; these directly show the stated penalty.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports declining VGG-16 validation accuracy as distributed training increases the global batch, but these comparisons remain unverified.
